# PR #4165: Patch: the dungeon run's shop and score strawmen hold run-sim affordability bands

Closes #4144

## What changed

`crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs` now has an economy-bands test beside the tiers test. `crates/run/**` is unchanged in the final diff.

- **`run-sim` output:** `Tally::render` appends economy lines after `Embers:` and leaves every old row alone. They are coins and tickets earned, shop visits, coins and tickets held entering a shop, the cheapest shop card, and the remove, Radiant and buff prices charged. `shop_visits` reads the prices by folding each run's log and calling `run_shop_prices`, so they are the prices actually charged after the relic discount.
- **`the_economy_holds_run_sims_bands`:**
  - It plays 24 stub-won runs (`ECONOMY_RUNS`, no AI) for coins, tickets and each run's first shop.
  - It plays `BAND_SEEDS` (6) whole AI runs for score and Embers, at the tiers test's seeds, `TEST_BUDGET` and full skill.
  - A pure function, `broken_economy`, names each broken band with its figures and the edit that breaks it. `render_economy` prints the table in the failure message.
- **Other tests:** `each_economy_band_names_the_edit_that_breaks_it` runs synthetic samples for each edit and for an empty sample. `the_tally_prints_the_economy_lines_after_the_old_rows` covers the render and `shop_visits`.
- **Docs:** the module header, the `run-sim` README row and the §15.13 "Measuring it" paragraph in `spec/15-dungeon-run.md`. No ruling.

## Measured, and the bands

Each band is the measured mean ÷2 (floored) to ×2, written in its const's doc comment.

| Figure | Measured | Band |
|---|---|---|
| Coins per won run | mean 707 (max 870) | 353..1414 |
| Tickets per won run | mean 43 (max 55) | 21..86 |
| AI score per run | mean 470 (max 1084) | 235..941 |
| AI Embers per run | mean 4 (max 10) | 2..8 |
| First shop reached | 22 of 24 runs | at least 50% |
| Cheapest shop card | mean 23 against 179 Coins held | at most 50% of Coins held |

The two affordability checks are relations, not measured bands. The median run must afford the cheapest card by its first shop. Its total Coins must cover that card plus one Remove, and its total Tickets one Radiant plus one buff.

## Tests run

- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim`: 17 passed, 1 ignored (the daily one), 63 s.
- The economy test alone takes about 41 s in a debug build on four cores. I noted that in the module header and the README row.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` and `cargo jackioh patches check` pass.
- `run-sim --seeds 2 --budget tiny` prints the old rows, then the new economy lines.
- I did not run the workspace-wide tests, the web tests or `classify`; the harness runs them.

## Acceptance edits tried in the real config, each reverted

- **`RUN_CARD_PRICE` ×10, all five rarities:** breaks "cannot afford the cheapest shop card… 120 held, 200 asked: RUN_CARD_PRICE or RUN_COINS" and "cheapest shop card costs … over 50%". Both name the edit, and nothing else breaks.
- **`RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER` 100 → 1000:** breaks exactly one band, "Embers per run 0 outside 2..8: RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER".
- **`RUN_COINS` zeroed:** breaks the coins band (220 against 353..1414) and the card-price ceiling. It does not break the "cannot afford" band, because chests and events still pay Coins.
- **Multiplying only the Common price by 10:** passes, because shops stock Rares too, so the cheapest card barely moves.

## Decisions and departures from the plan

- **AI runs are capped at 6 fights (`ECONOMY_AI_FIGHTS`).** The plan allowed this cap; uncapped, the test took 87 s. Score and Embers are measured on the capped runs, and the const's doc comment says so.
- **The tiers test plays single fights, not whole runs.** The plan said the AI part reuses its harness, but it can't, so the economy test uses `play_run` at the same seeds and budget instead.
- **Bands come from means.** The plan said to use the measured minimum and maximum. The test reads a mean per band, so I used mean ÷2 and ×2.
- **Zero coins breaks more than one band.** The synthetic zero-coins sample, where every coin figure is 0, breaks four bands (coins, afford, ceiling, Remove); the real edit breaks two. The acceptance text says "exactly its band", but that isn't possible here, and I did not special-case it in `broken_economy`.
- **Rejected:** retuning the strawman numbers directly, as the issue also rejected. Also rejected: raising the AI fights cap past the first mini-boss, which would cost much more test time.

## For the reviewer

- The score and Embers bands are an average of 6 AI runs of heavy-tailed score (max 1084 against mean 470). They are deterministic at the pinned seeds, but a legitimate AI or engine change can move them, and the failure message prints the table.
- `shop_visits` swallows `run_create` and `run_reduce` errors and returns what it gathered. Faulty runs are already reported through each run's `faults`, and the economy test returns `Err` on any fault.

# #4144: Patch: the dungeon run's shop and score strawmen hold run-sim affordability bands
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A dungeon run hands out coins and tickets, charges prices at shops and campfires, and turns score into a reward at the end. Many of those numbers are still rough guesses waiting for tuning. Once built, the test suite plays a handful of full runs with the practice opponent and fails when the economy clearly breaks, for example when an ordinary winning run can no longer afford the cheapest shop card, or when the end-of-run reward falls far outside its usual range. Players notice fair shops and meaningful rewards; the maintainer notices the breakage in a test message instead of in player complaints.

## Why

`crates/run/src/config.rs` marks the economy numbers as strawmen "to be tuned": `RUN_COINS`, `RUN_TICKETS`, `RUN_CARD_PRICE`, `RUN_ARTIFACT_PRICE`, `RUN_REMOVE_PRICE`, `RUN_RADIANT_TICKETS`, `RUN_BUFF_TICKETS`, plus the score row (`RUN_SCORE_ROW`, `RUN_SCORE_FIGHT`, `RUN_SCORE_DAMAGE`, `RUN_SCORE_HEALING`, `RUN_SCORE_CARD_DRAWN`, the boss percents, `RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER`) and `RUN_LEVEL_EMBERS`, all specified in `spec/15-dungeon-run.md` §§15.7, 15.8, 15.10 and 15.13. `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs` already prints wins, HP cost, rows reached, score by term and Embers per skill, but its only asserting test is `the_enemy_tiers_hold_run_sims_win_rate_bands` (`BAND_SEEDS = 6`, tier 1 at least 75% won, final boss at most 50% won, elites cost more HP). Nothing asserts the economy, so a price retune that makes shops decoration or Embers noise stays green.

## Proposal

Add an economy-bands test beside the tiers test, reusing its harness (`band_state`, `play_band_fight`/`play_match` at `TEST_BUDGET` and full skill, `KindTally`-style sums over `BAND_SEEDS` runs): tally coins and tickets earned over the first fights, the cheapest shop card, remove and Radiant prices actually charged, and the score-to-Embers payout of finished runs. Fail with a named band break (e.g. "median run cannot afford the cheapest shop card by its first shop" or "Embers per won run outside X..Y") and print the table as `render_bands` does. Keep bands wide because the header warns the AI plays better or worse than a person, so the table guides tuning rather than setting targets; a deliberate retune changes the bands in the same patch, as the tiers test already requires.

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/run_sim.rs`: new economy bands test and helpers beside `play_bands`, `broken_bands`, `render_bands`
- `crates/run/src/config.rs`: read only (values change only with a deliberate retune)
- SPEC sections read, not changed: §15.7 (packs, coins, tickets, drops), §15.8 (campfire, shop, prices), §15.10 (score and Embers), §15.13 (strawmen to tune); no new ruling since no rules decision changes

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The new test passes on the current strawmen at the same seeds and budget the tiers test uses.
- [ ] Multiplying `RUN_CARD_PRICE` (or zeroing `RUN_COINS`) breaks exactly its band with a message naming the edit, mirroring `each_band_names_the_tier_edit_that_breaks_it`.
- [ ] Pushing score payouts far outside their band (e.g. `RUN_SCORE_PER_EMBER` tenfold) breaks exactly its band.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh run_sim` stays within a noted time budget, and the daily `run-sim` text output keeps its old rows plus the new economy lines.

## Size and risks

Medium: one tools file plus its tests, no game-rules change. Main risks are flakiness and mistaking AI skill for human value; mitigate with the pinned `BAND_SEEDS` starts, `TEST_BUDGET`, seeded policy order, and wide bands. Rejected alternative: tuning the strawman numbers directly now; rejected because the starting lists are still placeholders (`placeholder.json`, `run_catalog_content`) and the AI baseline is not a human baseline, so bands-that-hold beat numbers-that-guess.
